name: Abijah (Abijam)
dom: Davidic continuity; war with Jeroboam I
note: Son of Rehoboam who warred against Jeroboam I and won at Mount Zemaraim, reigning three years.

name: Athaliah
dom: usurpation; Baalist purge of the Davidic line
note: Daughter of Ahab/Jezebel who seized Judah's throne after Ahaziah's death and slaughtered the royal heirs, ruling six years until executed by Jehoiada.

name: Jehoram (king of Judah)
dom: Omride marriage alliance; apostasy
note: Son of Jehoshaphat who married Athaliah, killed his brothers, lost Edom in revolt, and died of an incurable disease.

name: Ahaziah (king of Judah)
dom: Omride alliance; war against Aram
note: Son of Jehoram and Athaliah who reigned one year and was killed by Jehu during his revolt.

name: Joash (king of Judah)
dom: Temple repair; rescue of the Davidic line
note: Hidden as an infant from Athaliah and enthroned at seven by the priest Jehoiada; repaired the Temple but later apostatized and was assassinated.

name: Amaziah
dom: reconquest of Edom; defeat by Israel
note: Son of Joash who defeated Edom but was beaten and captured by Jehoash of Israel and later killed in a conspiracy at Lachish.

name: Jotham
dom: building projects; co-regency
note: Son of Uzziah who served as regent during his father's leprosy, built the Upper Gate of the Temple, and is judged generally righteous.

name: Amon (king of Judah)
dom: idolatry; brief reign cut short by assassination
note: Son of Manasseh who continued his father's idolatry and was assassinated by his servants after two years.

name: Jehoahaz (king of Judah)
dom: three-month reign; deposed by Egypt
note: Son of Josiah (Shallum) who reigned three months before Pharaoh Necho deposed him and carried him to Egypt, where he died.

name: Jehoiakim
dom: Egyptian then Babylonian vassalage; rebellion
note: Son of Josiah installed by Necho who became Nebuchadnezzar's vassal, rebelled, burned Jeremiah's scroll, and died as Babylon advanced.

name: Jehoiachin (Jeconiah)
dom: the first deportation; exile in Babylon
note: Son of Jehoiakim who reigned three months before surrendering in the 597 BCE deportation, later released from prison by Evil-merodach.

name: Nadab
dom: short reign; end of Jeroboam's house
note: Son of Jeroboam I who reigned two years before Baasha assassinated him at Gibbethon and wiped out his father's dynasty.

name: Baasha
dom: usurpation; war with Judah
note: Founder of his own house who seized the throne by killing Nadab, warred against Asa, and was condemned by the prophet Jehu son of Hanani.

name: Elah
dom: short reign ended by coup
note: Son of Baasha who reigned two years and was murdered while drunk by his chariot commander Zimri.

name: Zimri
dom: seven-day reign; suicide by fire
note: A chariot officer who killed Elah and reigned only seven days before Omri besieged him, whereupon he burned the palace over himself.

name: Tibni
dom: contested kingship; civil-war rival of Omri
note: Son of Ginath supported by half of Israel against Omri in a succession struggle, but his faction was defeated and he died.

name: Ahaziah (king of Israel)
dom: Baal worship; fatal fall
note: Son of Ahab who reigned two years, served Baal, and after falling through a lattice consulted Baal-zebub and died as Elijah foretold.

name: Jehoram (king of Israel)
dom: Moabite revolt; end of the house of Ahab
note: Son of Ahab (Joram) who fought Moab and Aram and was killed by Jehu during his coup, ending the Omride dynasty.

name: Jehoahaz (king of Israel)
dom: Aramean oppression; military decline
note: Son of Jehu whose reign saw Israel ground down by Hazael of Aram until only a remnant army remained.

name: Jehoash (king of Israel)
dom: recovery against Aram; defeat of Judah
note: Son of Jehoahaz (Joash) who recovered cities from Aram per Elisha's deathbed prophecy and defeated Amaziah of Judah.

name: Zechariah (king of Israel)
dom: six-month reign; end of the house of Jehu
note: Son of Jeroboam II who reigned six months before Shallum assassinated him, ending Jehu's dynasty in the fourth generation.

name: Shallum (king of Israel)
dom: one-month reign by assassination
note: Son of Jabesh who killed Zechariah and reigned a single month before Menahem struck him down.

name: Menahem
dom: brutal consolidation; Assyrian tribute
note: Son of Gadi who seized power by killing Shallum, sacked Tiphsah, and paid tribute to Pul (Tiglath-pileser III) of Assyria.

name: Pekahiah
dom: short reign ended by his captain's coup
note: Son of Menahem who reigned two years before his officer Pekah assassinated him in the citadel of Samaria.

name: Pekah
dom: the Syro-Ephraimite war; Assyrian invasion
note: Son of Remaliah who killed Pekahiah, allied with Rezin of Aram against Judah, lost much land to Tiglath-pileser III, and was killed by Hoshea.

name: Hoshea
dom: last king of Israel; the fall of Samaria
note: Final northern king who killed Pekah, became an Assyrian vassal but conspired with Egypt, and was imprisoned as Samaria fell and Israel was deported in 722 BCE.

name: Prochorus
dom: one of the Seven chosen to serve tables
note: One of the seven men of good repute appointed in Acts 6:5 to oversee the daily distribution to the Hellenist widows.

name: Nicanor
dom: one of the Seven chosen to serve tables
note: One of the seven deacons named in Acts 6:5, set apart by the apostles with prayer and the laying on of hands.

name: Timon
dom: one of the Seven chosen to serve tables
note: One of the seven deacons listed in Acts 6:5 to relieve the apostles of the daily ministration.

name: Parmenas
dom: one of the Seven chosen to serve tables
note: One of the seven deacons named in Acts 6:5 among those chosen to administer the church's daily distribution.

name: Nicolaus of Antioch
dom: one of the Seven; a proselyte of Antioch
note: The last-named of the seven deacons in Acts 6:5, identified as a proselyte from Antioch.

name: Cornelius (the centurion)
dom: the first Gentile convert; centurion of the Italian Cohort
note: A God-fearing centurion at Caesarea who, after a vision, was baptized by Peter and became the first Gentile convert (Acts 10).

name: Ananias of Damascus
dom: restored Saul's sight and baptized him
note: A disciple at Damascus sent in a vision to lay hands on Saul of Tarsus, restoring his sight and baptizing him (Acts 9:10-19).

name: Gamaliel
dom: the Pharisee teacher of the Law; teacher of Paul
note: A respected Pharisee who counseled restraint toward the apostles (Acts 5:34) and at whose feet Paul was educated (Acts 22:3).

name: Agabus
dom: Christian prophecy; foretelling famine and Paul's binding
note: A Christian prophet who foretold a great famine (Acts 11:28) and predicted Paul's arrest in Jerusalem (Acts 21:10-11).

name: Tabitha (Dorcas)
dom: charity and good works; raised from the dead
note: A disciple of Joppa known for charity and garment-making who was raised from the dead by Peter (Acts 9:36-42).

name: The Ethiopian eunuch
dom: treasurer of Candace; early African convert baptized by Philip
note: The treasurer of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was reading Isaiah when Philip explained the Scripture and baptized him (Acts 8:26-39).

name: Phoebe (deaconess)
dom: deaconess of Cenchreae; patron and bearer of Paul's letter to Rome
note: A deacon (diakonos) of the church at Cenchreae whom Paul commends as a benefactor and entrusts to the Roman church (Romans 16:1-2).

name: Junia
dom: kinswoman and fellow prisoner of Paul; noted among the apostles
note: A kinswoman and fellow prisoner of Paul, greeted in Romans 16:7 as outstanding among the apostles.

name: Onesimus
dom: the runaway slave of Philemon turned Christian helper of Paul
note: The slave of Philemon who, converted by Paul in prison, was sent back as a beloved brother (Philemon 10-16).

name: Philemon
dom: host of a house church at Colossae; master of Onesimus
note: A Christian of Colossae and host of a house church, addressed by Paul in the Epistle to Philemon on behalf of his slave Onesimus.

name: Epaphras
dom: evangelist of Colossae; fellow prisoner of Paul
note: A fellow servant who brought the gospel to Colossae and is named as Paul's fellow prisoner (Colossians 1:7; 4:12).

name: Onesiphorus
dom: refresher of Paul who sought him out in Rome
note: A supporter who often refreshed Paul and, unashamed of his chains, diligently sought him out in Rome (2 Timothy 1:16-18).

name: The Four Imams of the Sunni Schools of Law
dom: eponymous founders of the four Sunni madhhabs: Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali
note: Sunni Islam recognizes four orthodox schools of law, each named for a jurist of the 8th-9th centuries CE whose legal methodology it codified.

name: Abu Hanifa
dom: eponym of the Hanafi school; pioneer of ra'y and qiyas in fiqh
note: Abu Hanifa al-Nu'man ibn Thabit (c. 699-767 CE) of Kufa, eponymous founder of the Hanafi school, the most widely followed Sunni legal tradition.

name: Malik ibn Anas
dom: eponym of the Maliki school; compiler of the Muwatta; authority on Medinan practice
note: Malik ibn Anas (c. 711-795 CE) of Medina founded the Maliki school and authored the Muwatta, an early collection of hadith and law.

name: al-Shafi'i
dom: eponym of the Shafi'i school; systematizer of usul al-fiqh
note: Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i (767-820 CE) founded the Shafi'i school and is regarded as the father of Islamic legal theory in his Risala.

name: Ahmad ibn Hanbal
dom: eponym of the Hanbali school; traditionist and compiler of the Musnad
note: Ahmad ibn Hanbal (780-855 CE) of Baghdad founded the Hanbali school, emphasized hadith over speculative reasoning, and compiled the vast Musnad.

name: Talha ibn Ubaydullah
dom: early convert and warrior; shielded the Prophet at Uhud
note: One of the Ten Promised Paradise who famously shielded Muhammad at Uhud, sustaining wounds to his hand.

name: al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam
dom: early convert, cousin of the Prophet, cavalry commander
note: A paternal cousin of the Prophet and husband of Asma bint Abi Bakr, among the Ten Promised Paradise.

name: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf
dom: wealthy early convert and merchant; member of the shura
note: A prosperous early Muslim merchant, one of the Ten Promised Paradise, and a member of Umar's electoral council (shura).

name: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas
dom: commander; victory over the Sasanians at al-Qadisiyya
note: One of the Ten Promised Paradise who commanded the army that defeated the Sasanian Persians at al-Qadisiyya.

name: Sa'id ibn Zayd
dom: very early convert; brother-in-law of Umar
note: One of the Ten Promised Paradise, an early convert whose conversion (with his wife Fatima) preceded Umar's own.

name: Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah
dom: military commander; conquest of Syria; 'Trustee of this Nation'
note: One of the Ten Promised Paradise who commanded the conquest of Syria and was titled Amin al-Umma (Trustee of the Community).

name: Sawda bint Zam'a
dom: first wife after Khadijah's death; early convert and Abyssinian emigrant
note: The first woman Muhammad married after Khadijah's death, who had earlier emigrated to Abyssinia with her first husband.

name: Hafsa bint Umar
dom: daughter of Umar; keeper of the first written Qur'an
note: Daughter of the second caliph Umar, who kept the original compiled manuscript (suhuf) of the Qur'an after Abu Bakr.

name: Zaynab bint Jahsh
dom: cousin of the Prophet; her marriage referenced in Qur'an 33
note: The Prophet's cousin and formerly wife of his adopted son Zayd, whose marriage is addressed in Surah al-Ahzab.

name: Umm Salama
dom: noted hadith narrator and counselor at Hudaybiyya
note: Hind bint Abi Umayya, a prolific narrator of hadith credited with the advice that resolved the crisis at Hudaybiyya.

name: Juwayriya bint al-Harith
dom: daughter of a Banu Mustaliq chief; her marriage freed her tribe's captives
note: Daughter of the Banu Mustaliq chief; her marriage to the Prophet prompted Muslims to free their captives from her tribe.

name: Safiyya bint Huyayy
dom: of Jewish descent (Banu Nadir); married after Khaybar
note: A noblewoman of the Jewish Banu Nadir and daughter of its chief, who became the Prophet's wife after the Battle of Khaybar.

name: Umm Habiba
dom: emigrant to Abyssinia; daughter of Abu Sufyan
note: Ramla bint Abi Sufyan, daughter of the Quraysh chief Abu Sufyan, an emigrant to Abyssinia married to the Prophet by proxy of the Negus.

name: Maymuna bint al-Harith
dom: last woman the Prophet married; aunt of Ibn Abbas and Khalid
note: The last woman Muhammad married, wed during the fulfilled compensatory pilgrimage (umrat al-qada) of 7 AH.

name: Zaynab bint Khuzayma
dom: 'Mother of the Poor' (Umm al-Masakin); died soon after the marriage
note: Called Umm al-Masakin ('Mother of the Poor') for her generosity, she died only a few months after marrying the Prophet.

name: The Ninety-Nine Names of God (al-Asma al-Husna)
dom: the ninety-nine Beautiful Names and attributes by which God is invoked in Islam
note: Al-Asma al-Husna are the ninety-nine Beautiful Names of God (al-Rahman, al-Rahim, al-Malik, ...) enumerated in tradition and recited in devotion; names of the one God, not separate beings.
